content.title: About
content.content: Gelatin dessert with fruit is a sweet dish made from gelatin that incorporates pieces of fresh or canned fruit. The gelatin gives the dessert a light, wobbly texture, while the fruit adds natural sweetness, aroma, and a boost of vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The modern gelatin dessert became popular in Europe in the 19th century as a way to preserve fruit for longer periods.
Vegetarian and vegan alternatives to gelatin include agar‑agar and pectin.
The color of the dessert depends on the type of gelatin and the fruits used: strawberries yield a pink hue, oranges an orange tint.
Traditionally, gelatin desserts are served in small portions in cups or molded shapes.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruit pieces provide vitamin C, vitamin A and B‑complex vitamins, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Low‑calorie dessert
items.content: Gelatin desserts are low in fat and calories, making them suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Because gelatin is mostly water, it helps contribute to daily fluid intake.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Gelatin breaks down quickly in the stomach, making the dessert gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to gelatin derived from animal collagen.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercially prepared versions often contain added sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Artificial additives
items.content: Certain colorings and flavorings may cause sensitivity in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dessert chilled; garnish with fresh berries, mint leaves, or a sprinkle of nuts. It can be eaten directly from a cup or unmolded from a silicone mold using a spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared gelatin dessert in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑5 days. Over time, the flavor and texture may change.
